historical_record.description: Recorded in the city's survey of the Van Ness Avenue automobile corridor as built for use as an auto shop and garage. Dated 1917 and 1925. The first story was designed by Willis Polk and Company; the same firm added the second story in 1925, a year after Polk's death. It has profiled cornices, a chamfered corner at Eddy Street and a wooden classical entrance in the cornice. Three businesses at a time in its early years: auto repair shops from 1917, an auto painting shop 1918–1932, and a public garage 1919–1942. Later the whole building was one dealer's service shop.
A public garage ran in the building for 24 years from 1919.
Evaluated in the city's survey of the Van Ness Avenue automobile corridor and given California Register status code 3CS — individually eligible for the California Register, under Criteria 1 and 3.
